notes: Replaces every structural brace check in the dispenser and parser with quote-aware Token methods, matching the reference almost exactly. It misses the quoted-address `HasSuffix("{")` exemption and the quoted `"{}"` fall-through tweak, and leaves a now-redundant `wasQuoted` check and stale doc comments; the dispenser and parser tests it adds are solid.

C1 fixes the root cause: unquoted-brace helpers on Token replace every structural brace check in the dispenser and parser, it matches the reference closely, and its tests are solid, but it misses two small quoted-token refinements (the quoted address-suffix `{` check and quoted `"{}"` handling in directive()) and leaves a now-redundant wasQuoted check.

C1 fixes the reported same-module case: it returns every import block as a slice and dedups only across modules. However, a parent block that targets any instance of a child's resource (e.g. module.child.res["a"]) still silently discards all of the child's import blocks for that resource (e.g. res["b"]), the same silent-drop failure the issue complains about; the reference fixes this by deduping per instance at expansion time, and this gap likely explains the 2/3 hidden-test failures.

Fixes the reported same-module for_each case by appending all import blocks to a slice. It still dedups at the ConfigResource level across modules, so a child module's import for a different instance than the parent targeted is silently dropped. That is the same class of silent drop the issue describes, which the reference avoids by deduping per resource instance after expansion, and it likely explains failing 2 of 3 hidden tests.

The patch overlays a slugged SectionBase onto the existing section and container-dir logic and handles the main cases (sections, nested sections, bundles, taxonomies, terms), but it has edge-case bugs and costs: rebuilding the path from `path.Base` of each ancestor drops intermediate non-section directories, non-slug segments come from normalized paths so case is lost under disablePathToLower, and calling Ancestors().Reverse() for every page adds sort-cache overhead.

The patch applies section, taxonomy and term slugs to their own paths and to all descendant paths, and it passes the hidden tests. However, it rebuilds the path one segment per ancestor section using `path.Base`, so any intermediate directory without an `_index.md` drops out of the URL once a slug is present. It also builds those segments from normalized paths, so it ignores `disablePathToLower`, which the reference handles. Adding a parallel `SectionBase` field with `CutPrefix` fallbacks is less clean than the reference's single `Dir` field. The added test covers the issue example, a nested section slug, a taxonomy slug and a term page.

Adds `--once`, transforms the single, default or ambiguous scenario after consolidation, keeps exec/env/tags/options and rejects the conflicting shortcut flags, but it misses two edge cases: it does not drop shortcuts from lower layers before the merge, so an env/config duration or iterations can wipe the script's scenarios before `--once` runs, and it leaves the execution-segment flags unchecked and turns an unset exec into an explicit "default".

Adds `--once` cleanly after consolidation: it handles zero, one and multiple scenarios, rejects shortcut flags, preserves exec/env/tags/options and passes the hidden tests, but it has gaps the reference avoids.

Fixes the round-trip correctly by lifting a parenthesised NumberLiteral into a wrapped unary-plus DurationExpr, as the reference does, and adds the matching Pretty fix. It also keeps parse-time rejection of `foo[(0)]` and `foo[-(5s)]` through constantDurationValue, which the reference appears to lose. Minor issues: the wrapped node's start position points at the number rather than the opening paren, the unary path duplicates some logic, and the regenerated-file header line changed for no reason.

Fixes the root cause the same way as the reference: a parenthesised NumberLiteral is lifted into a Wrapped unary-plus DurationExpr, both in paren_duration_expr and in the wrapped unary path, and Pretty now omits unary plus to match String(); it also extends the positive_duration_expr check through unary wrappers so `foo[(0)]` and `foo[-(5s)]` keep their parse-time errors, which the reference does not do; tests are thorough (round-trip printer cases, updated AST expectations, error cases, promqltest evaluation); only blemishes are the regenerated goyacc header path and slightly duplicated wrapping logic.

The sentinel-error approach works for early returns in partials and regular templates, but it has several problems: a valued return in a non-partial is silently swallowed instead of erroring, and `walkTemplate` traps valued returns too, so values from `{{ template }}` inside partials are lost. It also adds no check for `return` placed mid-pipeline, keeps an AST rewrite (`wrapReturnArgs`), and edits upstream `exec.go` (`errRecover`/`walkTemplate`) without updating the fork script. It weakens an existing test's expected error to make it pass, the package suite fails, and orphaned doc comments are left behind.

Early return works in partials and regular templates via a sentinel error, but the patch has several problems: it edits upstream exec.go (errRecover, walkTemplate) without updating the fork script; it silently swallows valued returns in regular and `{{ template }}` contexts; it no longer rejects `return` in the middle of a pipeline; and it weakens an existing test assertion to match the new behavior, which the hidden suite catches.
